paragraphs.text: For even though all other people should escape, yet you will be punished.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: You have committed idolatry in hope of reward, and to have your barns filled ( Jer 44:17), as a harlot that had rather live by playing the whore, than to be provided for by her own husband.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: These outward things that you seek will be taken from you.
paragraphs.label: c
paragraphs.anchor: The floor and the winepress shall

paragraphs.text: All their doings both with regard to administration and religion, will be rejected as polluted things.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: The meat offering which they offered for themselves.
paragraphs.label: e
paragraphs.anchor: for their soul shall not come

paragraphs.text: When the Lord will take away all the occasions of serving him, which will be the most grievous part of your captivity, when you will see yourselves cut off from God.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Even though they think to escape by fleeing the destruction that is at hand, yet they will be destroyed in the place where they flee for help.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: Then they will know that they were deluded by those who claimed themselves to be their prophets and spiritual men.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: The Prophet's duty is to bring men to God, and not to be a snare to pull them from God.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: This people is so rooted in their wickedness, that Gibeah, which was similar to Sodom, was never more corrupt; Jud 19:22.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: Meaning, that he esteemed them and delighted in them in this way.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: They were as abominable to me, as their lovers the idols.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: Signifying that God would destroy their children by these different means, and so consume them by little and little.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: As they kept tender plants in their houses in Tyrus to preserve them from the cold air of the sea, so was Ephraim at the first to me: but now I will give him to the slaughter.
paragraphs.label: o

paragraphs.text: The Prophet seeing the great plagues of God toward Ephraim, prays to God to make them barren, rather than that this great slaughter should come upon their children.
paragraphs.label: p

paragraphs.text: The chief cause of their destruction is that they commit idolatry, and corrupt my religion in Gilgal.
paragraphs.label: q
